items.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
items.desc: CISA has added one new vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2026-110447 Collabora Online – Built-in CODE Server OS Command Injection Vulnerability This type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and poses significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria . Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form . Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

Read More 3 Affected Products InterSystems Corporation InterSystems IRIS for Health: 2026.2.0.221 Product Status: known_affected Remediations Mitigation InterSystems recommends users configure IRIS superserver to require SSL/TLS: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=ROARS_gsecuring_checklist Note that there are three settings: "Disabled", which means that client communications do not use TLS. items.title: Managing AI Token Consumption for Operational Resilience
items.desc: CISA, the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre), and partners are releasing joint guidance, Managing AI Token Consumption for Operational Resilience , to help organizations understand and manage token usage in support of operations. As organizations adopt third-party super intelligence (SI) services, token-based usage models can affect cost, performance, and access to critical services. Unmanaged token consumption may contribute to rising and unpredictable costs, reduced service availability, degraded performance, token exhaustion, and denial-of-tokens or denial-of-wallet attacks. The guidance outlines practical steps organizations can take to prioritize token allocation, design efficient workflows, improve user prompting practices, leverage caching and reusable context, optimize data before submission, and monitor token consumption over time. Critical infrastructure owners and operators can use this guidance to identify mission-critical functions that depend on SI, understand service provider and operational dependencies, and plan for reduced SI availability during outages, incidents, or periods of high demand. Cyber defenders can also use the guidance to manage SI-enabled cyber defense workflows while maintaining human oversight, governance, and strong cybersecurity fundamentals.

items.title: CISA Urges Patching Critical Vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support
items.desc: CISA is aware of critical authentication bypass vulnerability CVE-2026-102764 , affecting BeyondTrust Remote Support (formerly Bomgar) versions 26.2.3 and earlier. Patches are available for supported versions (24.3.1 and later); organizations using older versions must upgrade first. Cyber threat actors are actively exploiting the vulnerability to gain initial access, then establishing persistence, escalating privileges, and moving laterally. CISA added CVE-2026-102764 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on Oct. 16, 2026. CISA urges organizations with affected self-hosted Remote Support appliances to immediately take the following actions: Apply the BT26-05-RS patch, as outlined in BeyondTrust’s Security Advisory BT26-05 . Organizations on a self-hosted Remote Support version older than 24.3.1 will need to upgrade to a newer version to apply the patch. Organizations using BeyondTrust-hosted (SaaS) Remote Support deployments have already been patched. Review BeyondTrust’s blog ARMORY CASTLE and BT26-05: What Security Teams Need to Know for detailed information on the vulnerability and recommended response and mitigation actions. Limit external access to the Remote Support appliance to the services needed to support users and customers. Restrict access to administrative interfaces to trusted networks. Review BeyondTrust’s B Series Appliance on-premises security for additional guidance on securing network connectivity for self-hosted Remote Support appliances. Organizations with affected self-hosted Remote Support appliances should conduct network and memory forensics to identify evidence of potential compromise. If your organization suspects a compromise, CISA recommends taking the following actions: Isolate any suspected or confirmed compromised appliance
